_note: Normal breast histologic structures for CoD-MIL's second diagnostic chain (normal-tissue exclusion). CoD-MIL publishes a normal-tissue bank only for kidney (rows 7-12 of prompt/text_prompt_kidney_v2.csv are organ-specific; rows 13-27 are organ-independent and are reused verbatim from background_tissue_generic.json). These breast equivalents are authored for this benchmark in the released bank's voice and are NOT upstream assets: a CoD-MIL result on BRCA is therefore not prompt-faithful and must be reported as such.
prompts: This is an image of terminal duct lobular units which appear as clustered small acini grouped around a central intralobular duct, each lined by a inner cuboidal epithelial layer and an outer myoepithelial layer, set in loose specialised intralobular stroma.

This is an image of large lactiferous ducts which appear as branching tubular profiles lined by a two-cell-layer epithelium, often with a folded or undulating luminal contour and a surrounding cuff of denser periductal collagen.

This is an image of the myoepithelial layer which appears as a continuous outer rim of flattened to cuboidal cells with clear or eosinophilic cytoplasm lying between the luminal epithelium and the basement membrane of ducts and acini.

This is an image of interlobular fibrous stroma which appears as broad bands of densely packed, paucicellular collagen separating lobular units, containing scattered fibroblasts and few inflammatory cells.
This is an image of breast adipose tissue which appears as sheets of large clear univacuolated adipocytes with compressed peripheral nuclei and delicate intervening fibrovascular septa.

This is an image of normal breast vasculature and lymphatics which appear as thin-walled channels lined by a single layer of flattened endothelium, some containing red blood cells and others optically empty.
